findings.title: Old-password login could survive concurrent account recovery
findings.reproduction: Pause password_verify immediately after successful old-password derivation; complete recovery in a second client; resume login. Original implementation inserted a new valid session after recovery had revoked all sessions.
findings.fix: After password verification, BEGIN IMMEDIATE and re-fetch current password hash. Compare exact verified encoding; reject if changed before inserting session.
findings.check: test_login_cannot_survive_concurrent_password_recovery passed independently; stale login returns401 and no session cookie.

findings.title: Signing in as another account after expiry displayed previous owner's private browser state

findings.fix: Clear all owner-scoped UI state, drafts, request IDs, microphone/audio work and pending async operations on account transition. Compare immutable user.id rather than reusable username; clear on missing identity. Same-account reauthentication preserves drafts but invalidates old async operations; ownerEpoch rejects late responses.

findings.title: Rate-limited anonymous requests still grew persistent attempt records
findings.location: production.py: login, recover, record_rate; production_store.py: attempts indexes
findings.reproduction: After login-ip quota is exhausted, POST different valid-format unknown usernames. Original username limiter ran before IP limiter, inserting a new row on every blocked request; cleanup scanned an unindexed timestamp.
findings.fix: Check IP quota first; cap attempt table at50000 rows; index occurred; fail closed at capacity.
findings.check: security_review_v3_proof.py: first40 requests401, next15 requests429, final10 denied requests add0 records (80→80). Existing blocked-IP/cap regression independently passed.

findings.title: Concurrent recovery did not stop an already verified old-password account deletion
findings.reproduction: Pause delete-account password verification after success; recover account with one-use code; release deletion. Original code deleted account without checking that session/password remained current.
findings.fix: Revalidate live session and exact verified password hash inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE before deletion.
findings.check: test_account_deletion_cannot_survive_concurrent_recovery passed independently; account survives stale deletion.

findings.title: Audio admission could race account deletion, and commit failure could leak global audio permit
findings.reproduction: Authenticate audio before account deletion, then delay begin_audio until deletion finishes; original admission trusted stale auth and registered work. A DB COMMIT failure after acquiring AUDIO_LOCK also lacked cleanup.
findings.fix: Admission rechecks live session transactionally; both paths take database write lock then AUDIO_JOBS_LOCK; deletion holds jobs lock through commit. Failed admission commit removes registry entry and releases semaphore.
findings.check: test_audio_cannot_start_after_account_deletion passed independently. Synthetic SQLite COMMIT failure probe confirmed registry entry removal and audio semaphore availability. Consistent lock ordering inspected in source; cross-account cancellation test passed.

findings.title: Deleted mission retries and expired logins could accumulate unbounded metadata
findings.reproduction: Repeat new mission request IDs followed by deletion to bypass the200-active-mission cap while retaining creation_requests forever. Repeated successful logins retained expired auth_sessions indefinitely.
findings.fix: Cap creation markers at10000/account, new creation at60/hour/account after deduplication, purge expired sessions and retain at most10 active sessions/account. Preserve tombstones so deletion cannot be undone by stale retry.
findings.check: test_creation_tombstones_are_bounded, test_new_mission_rate_excludes_retries, test_sessions_expire_and_are_capped all passed independently.

findings.title: Legacy import accepted non-standard numeric JSON before raw streaming
findings.reproduction: Python json.loads accepts object payloads containing NaN or Infinity; raw history streaming would send those tokens as invalid browser JSON. Overflow numbers such as1e999 also become nonfinite in the parser.
findings.fix: Reject parse_constant values and validate decoded object with json.dumps(...,allow_nan=False) before insertion. Reject non-object, malformed, oversize and over-count inputs atomically.
findings.check: Independent targeted legacy-import tests passed: trusted import plus all-or-nothing rejection cases. Source caps200 records/account,128KiB UTF-8 bytes/record,128-character IDs and validates all input before the write transaction.

changes.problem: Stopping/renaming the old container and copying rollback data outside recovery handling could leave the service down.
changes.fix: Fsynced operation journal before cutover; recover by immutable old container ID after update/stop/rename/backup/start failure. Retry recovers interrupted operations; completed operation cleanup never rolls back a healthy committed service.
changes.evidence: Fault tests cover update, stop, rename, encrypted snapshot and startup failures; original container restarts with previous restart policy.

changes.problem: Restoring a pre-release SQLite copy could erase requests accepted by the new release before a late rollout failure.
changes.fix: Never overwrite the active database. Take encrypted ordinary recovery backup while old service is stopped; restart old container against preserved active data. No new plaintext rollback.sqlite3.
changes.evidence: Synthetic new-user write survives failed new startup and old-container recovery. Legacy fixed-name snapshot is never replayed.

changes.problem: Old source fingerprint omitted build inputs and broad archive scanning admitted unrelated job outputs; extraction and source path boundaries were weak.
changes.fix: Exact runtime allowlist, bounded bytes, manifest hash for every uploaded file, pre/post source comparison, symlink/junction/hardlink rejection, bounded tar member validation, immutable verified release directory and activation-time revalidation.
changes.evidence: Scope exclusion, Dockerfile hash change, mid-package change, remote tamper and path traversal tests pass. Source-mode preparation preserves nonroot Docker COPY readability inside private release parent.

changes.problem: Resolving backup path before checking links hid symlinks; backup location could target other managed files; partial encryption and failed backup retention were not handled.
changes.fix: Validate lexical path components and SQLite sidecars before opening; allow only active data directory; serialize backups; clean abandoned plaintext; encrypt to unique partial file then atomically publish; prune expired encrypted files even when new encryption fails; publish failed backup status.
changes.evidence: Atomic success/failure, no leftover plaintext/partial output, active data preservation, incorrect-target rejection and failure-time retention tests pass. Actual Linux symlink test awaits root.

changes.problem: Cancelled SSH/builds could leave unmanaged children and uncertain remote rollout state.
changes.fix: Terminate and reap local SSH child, request per-operation remote cancellation marker, check cancellation around bounded subprocesses, terminate build process group, journal recovery. Network checkpoint every30seconds; initial/final checks remain.
changes.evidence: Offline cancelled-transfer and cancelled-build child cleanup tests pass. Network outage cannot guarantee remote receipt; retry/operator must inspect journal.

changes.problem: Failed or interrupted candidate clones could retain account copies beyond the backup policy.
changes.fix: Clean candidate copies independently of old-service recovery once unused. Daily backup invokes six-day expiry under nonblocking deployment lock, checks all active container mounts, rejects links, expires only known private clone/recovery namespaces, retains expiry metadata. Active data is never a cleanup target.
changes.evidence: Old inactive clone expires; active mounted clone and production database remain; operation journal and maintenance history record expiry.

remaining_limits: Root must verify Linux fcntl/symlink behavior, uid996 ownership, Docker lifecycle, Caddy route, actual age encryption/decryption/restore and timer execution; offline mocks do not establish these.

Automatic container rollback requires backward-compatible database migrations. No automatic database restoration can discard accepted writes; an incompatible migration requires operator recovery using the encrypted backup and off-server key.

Hard kill, host failure or complete SSH loss may leave an interrupted journal until next activation. The deploy lock serializes recovery; cancellation cannot be guaranteed when the host is unreachable.

The <=7-day policy relies on a functioning daily timer using the six-day cutoff. Maintenance retains artifacts with active container mounts, unsafe paths, missing modern journals or unavailable Docker inventory and reports the reason; operator monitoring must address those conditions.
Release source/image caches and stopped previous containers are metadata/software artifacts, not automatically pruned here. Operator disk-capacity maintenance remains necessary.
No public-anonymous launch claim: the reviewed service remains invitation-only real accounts on the existing VPS.
